_why: THE BACKUP DESTINATIONS AS DATA, each set with a restore drill. Read by tooling/ops/restore-drill.mjs (one named small file from the newest snapshot into a scratch directory, hashed against the hash the SOURCE recorded, then deleted), by tooling/ops/box-move.mjs (the backups to restore first, with a drill command each) and by tooling/ops/check-box-declared.mjs (`readBack`: the snapshot count and the newest timestamp of a repository that lives on a box).

TRAP backup-04: a restructure that renames AND relayouts gets half-applied, so every destination declares BOTH its remote NAME and its LAYOUT. A `<NAME>` inside a remote or repository is an environment variable the operator sets from the vault; the drill reports LOST when it is unset and never prints its value.

TRAP backup-06: a same-day re-run of a date-stamped backup replaces that day's artefact, so the drill READS and never runs a backup. Restic is always called with --no-lock (a lock is a write to the repository).

The encryption posture is cited per destination ([ADR 021], [ADR 046], [ADR 047], [ADR 060]); the facts are those of tooling/ops/register.json rows duty.restic-snapshot, duty.restic-third-copy, duty.cloudflare-backup-pull and duty.supabase-dump, cited by id, not restated beyond the name and the layout.

A field the public tree does not state is null. A drill whose `file` or `hash` is null is LOST, by design: naming the small file and where its hash was recorded is the first drill's work, never a guess.

encryption.posture: restic's own repository encryption; the repository key never leaves the box
restic's repository key inside the rclone crypt `oracleenc:` on the company Drive: the provider holds ciphertext twice over
restic's repository key over R2 (restic's native S3 backend: rclone serve restic --stdio is refused by R2 with 501)

a byte copy of /srv/restic through the rclone crypt `ocienc:` (the same obscured key as `oracleenc:`) into the versioned OCI bucket nikatru-backup-thirdcopy; the box's credential holds no delete right
no client-side encryption is declared for the objects: the export is gzip inside Cloudflare, and the off-vendor copy (drive-cloudflare) is the encrypted one
the rclone crypt `oracleenc:` on the company Drive
plaintext on the box's own disk; the off-box copies are the encrypted ones
the Drive sync of gt_drive_sync.sh (duty.oci.gt-drive-sync); its remote name and layout are not stated in the public tree
plaintext on the box's own disk; the off-box copies are the encrypted ones
the Drive sync of sb_drive_sync.sh (duty.supabase-drive-sync); its remote name and layout are not stated in the public tree
the second copy sb_boxb_sync.sh pushes to Box B (duty.supabase-second-copy); its path is not stated in the public tree

sets.what: The seven paths of /opt/backup/restic-sets.txt on Box B, after sqlite-snapshot.py, tagged boxb,daily.
sets.retention: Sundays: forget --keep-daily 14 --keep-weekly 8 --keep-monthly 6 --prune on all three repositories

sets.what: An rclone copy of /srv/restic into the OCI Object Storage bucket through `ocienc:`; a superset of /srv/restic (the weekly prune does not reach it).
sets.retention: none upstream: the copy only grows; reconciling it is a deliberate act with the tenancy admin key

sets.what: The nightly pg_dump of GlitchTip's database, then its Drive sync (duty.oci.gt-drive-sync).
Four artefacts every six hours: the globals, the postgres and _supabase databases, and the pgsodium root key; then the Drive sync and the second copy to Box B.

The nightly D1 and KV export the platform Worker writes to R2 (services/platform/src/backup/index.ts), with a manifest that records every object's SHA-256; Box B's cf_backup_pull.sh copies it off-vendor (duty.cloudflare-backup-pull).
sets.retention: R2: the Worker's retentionDays (isExpired in services/platform/src/backup/index.ts); the Drive copy: 35 days
